description: RUBEM is a pixel-based hydrological model developed at the University of São Paulo for estimating surface and subsurface runoff. It applies monthly water-balance calculations to vegetated, bare, water and impervious land-cover fractions, with root and saturated zones and flow direction from a digital elevation model. Users provide raster rainfall, climate, land cover, terrain and configuration parameters; outputs are spatial water-balance states and accumulated streamflow for the chosen basin. Pixel size is flexible and the time step is monthly. Source is free under GPL-3.0-or-later, with installation guidance and documentation for Python, PCRaster and GDAL. A limitation is that monthly steps cannot resolve a short urban storm pulse or detailed sewer hydraulics. Performance also depends on terrain and remotely sensed vegetation inputs for the selected period. RUBEM supports basin supply and land-use change simulations. The catalogue's model-raven is a separate hydrological framework for comparison; no common basin run was checked. No raster data or package was downloaded.
inputs: Rainfall, climate, land cover and terrain rasters
